record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can knowledge-base profiling and mining improve mapping quality by using available or automatically inferred constraints, such as cardinality constraints, functional-property constraints, inverse-functional-property constraints, disjointness constraints, join paths, or other mined dependencies, to resolve ambiguous property-path choices in source-to-target mappings?

evidence.quote: In general, we feel that KB profiling and mining may be helpful in improving mapping quality, in a similar way that database profiling and dependency mining [1] has been used to mine for join paths or other constraints that can guide mapping generation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a source knowledge base S and a target knowledge base T each be specified as a set of typed entities together with a finite set of binary properties; a property path in T is a finite composition p_1 ∘ p_2 ∘ ... ∘ p_k of such properties. A source-to-target mapping is a function that assigns, to each source attribute or relation, a property path in T whose evaluation produces values of the intended type. A mapping is called ambiguous when several distinct property paths in T are type-compatible candidates for the same source attribute.

Consider the following classes of integrity constraints that may either be declared in T or be inferred automatically from instance data in T by profiling/mining procedures:
  (i) cardinality constraints on properties,
  (ii) functional-property constraints (a property is single-valued on its domain),
  (iii) inverse-functional-property constraints (the inverse is single-valued),
  (iv) disjointness constraints between classes or properties,
  (v) join-path constraints (e.g., approximate or exact inclusion dependencies between compositions of properties),
  (vi) more general mined dependencies (such as conditional functional dependencies or denial constraints).

Develop a formal framework in which such constraints are used to filter or rank candidate property paths in T for each source attribute, and prove that there exists a constraint-driven disambiguation procedure that, given any source-to-target mapping instance with at least one ambiguous property-path choice, produces a unique or strictly smaller set of candidate property paths whose induced mapping has provably higher quality (under a precisely defined quality measure, e.g., preservation of source dependencies, consistency with target constraints, and faithfulness to instance data) than mappings produced without using the constraints.

Equivalently: determine whether automatically inferred constraints of types (i)–(vi) are sufficient, in general, to resolve ambiguous property-path choices in source-to-target mappings and thereby improve mapping quality, and characterize the conditions on S, T, and the constraint set under which such improvement can be guaranteed.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a forward-looking research direction concerning whether knowledge-base profiling and constraint mining can disambiguate property-path choices in schema/ontology mappings. No general formal solution or guarantee theorem appears in the literature; existing works on profiling, dependency mining, and ontology mapping (e.g., approaches using functional/inverse-functional properties, disjointness axioms, and inclusion/join-path dependencies) address restricted cases but do not provide a general answer. The status is best regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open-problems survey discussing profiling-driven constraints for mapping quality.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented among open problems and research directions rather than resolved results.
